digest.component_or_area: live Jira Data Center integration tests
propositions: The provenance test assertion greps for the raw Jira key (e.g. RBJNAZV-1) as a substring in json.dumps(ticket), but the local ticket id is lowercased (jira-rbjnazv-1) and the raw key does not appear in the payload, so the match cannot succeed even when inbound create works correctly.

The inbound create path does not carry the raw Jira key in the ticket payload except as a fallback summary, so it is absent whenever the issue has a summary; the actual DC-to-local correspondence is recorded in the binding store, which list_tickets does not return.
The test must assert against the exact local id derived from _jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key) using an equality check, not a substring scan, to properly validate ticket creation.
The test must additionally assert that the binding store maps the local id to the remote_key, since that is where the genuine DC-to-local correspondence lives.
This defect is the third oracle-that-cannot-pass in the epic, following a pattern where live tests were authored against assumed output shapes rather than what the code actually emits.

The headline AC for the inbound half — 'an issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass' — remains unproven until the oracle assertions are corrected to match the actual payload structure.
